correctness.rationale: The canonical zero-sum symmetric edge polytope has width w_G(U)=2 max_edges |U_i-U_j|. Gaussian normalization gives (sqrt(n-1)/2)w_G(U)=D_G(g)(1+o_P(1/log n)) uniformly over graphs, since b_n^2=O(log n). Opposite Gaussian extreme processes converge jointly to independent intensity exp(-x)dx Poisson processes; independent ER edge marks survive on every finite extreme window. The Poisson no-edge probability for all crosspairs above level t reduces, conditional on upper exp-transformed arrivals S_k, to exp(-e^(-t) sum_k p(1-p)^(k-1)/S_k). This produces H+log A_p, with A_p>0 finite. For any fixed t the change to f_n(G)=P_g(D_G<=2b_n+t/b_n) upon one edge flip is at most q_n=O(sqrt(log n)/n^2). McDiarmid yields exp(-c n^2/log n) graph concentration, summable for arbitrary couplings of ER marginals. Rational t and continuity yield almost-sure quenched weak convergence. The maximal and minimal Gaussian labels form one uniformly random unordered pair, proving exact coincidence probability |E|/binom(n,2). Splitting A_p=p/S_1+B with E B=-p log p yields sharp upper tail p t exp(-t). The finite 5-vertex exhaustive verification in supplied checker and independent simulation are diagnostic only.
residual_risks: Fixed p in (0,1], canonical zero-sum Euclidean embedding, quenched weak distribution for almost every graph sequence; excludes p_n->0 and deterministic edge-density-only hypotheses.

originality.rationale: Chen–Davis–Korchevskaia classify symmetric-edge-polytope facets via graph subgraphs, Braun–Bruegge–Kahle analyze random facet-supporting hyperplanes, and Donzelmann et al. establish CLTs for counts of edges/triangulation edges. None of the inspected theorems concerns uniform-DIRECTION spherical widths or derives the marked two-Gaussian-extreme Gumbel mixture and almost-sure graph quenched law. Exact deterministic coincidence probability is a useful component, but the central novelty is the complete second-order width distribution.
residual_risks: An unindexed work on Gaussian-labeled ER-graph maxima could subsume the marked extreme-process mechanism. The known facet/face results do not settle directional widths.
